stills.prompt: Low-key interior: a near-black stone workshop with almost no ambient light. On a worn charcoal stone workbench stand two small horizontal mill engines side by side, both in profile, the same size and outline, each with its cylinder at the left end and the black iron six-spoke flywheel from @wheel at the right end. The left engine is the worn working original: aged-gold (#C6A94F) brass cylinder and crosshead on a black iron bed, brass dulled at the edges, a thin oil sheen. The right engine is a cast replica of it in solid dark bronze, one single uniform dull-brown metal from base to flywheel, every part fused, like a museum casting. One cool bone-white (#F5F2EB) light rakes from high left and draws a bright edge along both flywheel rims; everything else falls off into black. No windows, no white walls. No people, no lettering. Restrained, photorealistic, natural film grain.
